data.long_meaning: Ardyce is derived from the Greek name Ardia, which means ‘mountain goat’ or ‘strong as a lioness’. It was also a common name in ancient Greece for a goddess of the hunt. In Christian tradition, it is believed to represent strength and courage. The name Ardyce carries the meaning “Strong as a lioness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ardyce usually hope their child will grow to embody strong as a lioness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: ** Ardyce was uncommon as a given name in the English-speaking world, but it gained popularity in the United States in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. It is believed that the name became fashionable due to its association with the literary character Ardice Forrester in the novel "Armadale" by Wilkie Collins. The name also appears in contemporary popular culture in the form of the nickname "Ardy" for Ardis, shortening the name to a modern and trendy form.
data.spiritual_significance: ** In Christian tradition, the name Ardyce is believed to symbolize strength and courage, as it was derived from the Greek name Ardia, meaning 'mountain goat' or 'strong as a lioness'. The name reflects the biblical concept of being strong in faith, as defined in 1 Peter 5:9: "Resist him, standing firm in your faith, knowing that the same afflictions are being experienced by your brothers and sisters in all the world." Additionally, Ardyce's association with the goddess of the hunt may also signify the spiritual journey of life as a pursuit of righteousness and truth, as defined in Psalm 25:5: "Guide me in your truth and teach me, for you are God my Savior, and my hope is in you all day long."
